listen: Good morning. This is The Daily Brief for Thursday, November 26. Our lead story is about mathematics and AI. Science News reports that the Riemann hypothesis appears to be solved. It is a 167-year-old puzzle related to prime numbers. The proof comes from a human mathematician working with AI. The word apparently matters here, so treat it as an early report. Now the front page. A federal judge has blocked the Trump administration from moving to review all local broadcast licenses held by ABC. Those stations air in six of the largest U.S. markets. The FCC has also given SpaceX approval to deploy one million satellites for data centers in space. Scientists have expressed skepticism. In sports, Kevin Durant scored 20 points and became the fifth player in NBA history to reach 33,000 points. The Houston Rockets beat the Phoenix Suns 116 to 104. And 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy sat out Wednesday's practice with an ankle injury suffered against the Vikings. Now the sections. In tech and AI, a Claude Code skill bundle for bug hunting is trending on GitHub. A history professor describes GPT 6.2 Astra identifying the creator of an anonymous 1808 sketchbook. And Anthropic says its AI for Science program now reaches foundations and research institutions. In politics, The Lever reports on a bill that could fast-track pipelines, data centers and fossil fuel projects. Drop Site News reports that clients of a Pentagon official's family firm won up to three and a half billion dollars in contracts. In world news, the text of the new UK and EU treaties is due this afternoon, and the deal has a ten-year termination clause. A rights group says women are being sentenced to death in Iran in numbers not seen for decades. In Indonesia, thirteen people are dead and thirteen missing after an illegal gold mine flooded. In sports, the 49ers activated cornerback Nate Hobbs from injured reserve. The Braves face a shortstop question for 2027. And two UFC light heavyweights from New Zealand will not fight each other for the title. In Atlanta, Governor-elect Keisha Lance Bottoms will be inaugurated on January 12 at State Farm Arena. Two Georgia House Republicans are challenging their November defeats. And the Gemini project in Reynoldstown has started topping out. In architecture, Nomic is bringing AI agents into Revit and AutoCAD. Motif's vision for agentic BIM modeling is explained. And ArchDaily looks at who designed the world's heaviest building in Bucharest. In science and nature, astronomers are studying a nearby supernova caught in early November. Nations welcomed new Atlantic shark finning rules. And Hubble has surveyed an ocean of stars to prepare for the Roman Space Telescope. That is the brief. Have a good day.

lead.title: Math’s holy grail, the Riemann hypothesis, appears solved with AI’s help
lead.note: Science News reports that a 167-year-old puzzle about prime numbers, the Riemann hypothesis, appears to have been solved. The proof is credited to a human mathematician working with AI. The summary says the work apparently settles the problem, so the wording is cautious and the result is not described as confirmed. Even so, the item calls the Riemann hypothesis math's holy grail, and a settled answer would be a notable moment for the field. For a reader who builds software tools with AI, the story shows a person and a model working together on a long-standing problem. The item gives no further detail about the method or who did the work, so follow-up reporting will matter. Treat it as an early report, and wait for other mathematicians to weigh in.
lead.headline: Riemann Hypothesis Appears Solved With AI's Help
decks: Proof apparently settles a 167-year-old puzzle about prime numbers.
A human mathematician worked with AI on the result.
